clue.text: Gave feedback, loving to be abusive

parts.note: gave food is FED, and 'feed back' asks for those letters turned round
amatory means relating to love, loving

explanation.surface: Someone responded with affection to a person who turned out to be insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feedback' splits into 'feed' + 'back': 'Gave feed' is FED, and 'back' turns it into DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamatory language attacks a reputation, so it is insulting and abusive.

clue.text: Made unusually broad

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the neighbouring word set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something was made exceptionally wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad' is old slang for a woman, as is DAME in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated American slang for a woman.

clue.text: Distance coat extended

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
extended means long, drawn out

explanation.surface: A coat lengthened by some way.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is a unit of length, an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing.

clue.text: Exceptional skill needed to become butterfly expert, say

parts.note: an expert is a master
butterfly is one kind of swimming stroke, as 'say' marks it an example

explanation.surface: A lepidopterist needs real brilliance to reach the top of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly' suggests insects; it is the swimming stroke, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is a brilliantly skilful move or idea.

clue.text: Deceives one's successor on paper

parts.note: the number that follows one is two
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A deputy betrays someone in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to cheat on a partner, deceiving them.

clue.text: State singer gets part in Venice

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
an alto is a singer with a low voice

explanation.surface: A national singer lands a role in a Venetian production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a role; it is a district of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is a well-known district of Venice with its famous bridge.

clue.text: Report a disaster in magazine

explanation.surface: A news story covers a catastrophe in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: A magazine is also a store for gunpowder, where a disaster would be an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sound of a gun or explosion, and an explosion in an ammunition store makes a loud noise.

clue.text: In which to find elite involved in art, endlessly?

definitions.text: In which to find elite involved in art, endlessly?

indicators.note: in places one set of letters within the shortened word
endlessly means the word art loses its final letter
involved means tangled up, so the letters of elite are mixed

explanation.surface: Where does the artistic elite gather?
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ART to AR, and 'involved' turns ELITE into TELIE, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio, where the art world's best would work.

clue.text: Reserve keeper in match Septimus Harding

parts.note: a match is a game
Septimus Harding is the hero of Trollope's novel The Warden

explanation.surface: A substitute goalkeeper plays a match alongside a Trollope character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve keeper' suggests a spare goalkeeper; it is someone who looks after a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden protects the wildlife of a park or reserve.

clue.text: One aiming to be an examiner? Not he

indicators.note: not he says the male part of the word is replaced with a female one

parts.note: an examiner is someone who marks papers, a marks-man

explanation.surface: A candidate hopes to become an examiner, and she is not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A markswoman is a skilled female shooter, who aims at targets.

clue.text: Ray's major fault in sight

explanation.surface: Raymond's big flaw is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is from the Bible: the beam in your own eye compared with the mote in your brother's.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a ray of light, and in the Sermon on the Mount a beam in one's eye is a big personal failing.

clue.text: Smooth out trenchant piece taken from paper

parts.note: to press cloth is to smooth it out
trenchant means sharp, cutting

explanation.surface: Flatten a sharp article clipped from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an article clipped from a newspaper.

clue.text: Author's life companion

explanation.surface: A writer's partner for life.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Hope wrote The Prisoner of Zenda; 'while there's life there's hope' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope is a novelist, and the proverb pairs life with optimism.

clue.text: Audience for part of chat show

explanation.surface: The studio audience is part of a talk show.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal meeting with someone important, and a chat show is built from conversations with guests.

clue.text: Some players certain to follow captain in play

indicators.note: to follow places the second piece after the first

parts.note: the brass are the trumpet and horn players of an orchestra
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Musicians are sure to back the lead in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Brassbound is the title character of Shaw's play Captain Brassbound's Conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassbound is the captain in Shaw's comedy.

clue.text: To show regret is strange

indicators.note: strange means odd, so these letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Displaying remorse is an odd thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To show regret' looks like a phrase; 'To show' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To register a feeling is to display it, as a face registers surprise.

clue.text: Sort of shark you pronounced more trustworthy

indicators.note: pronounced means the word you is given by its spoken form, a single letter

parts.note: you is spoken the same as the letter U
surer means more reliable

explanation.surface: Somebody calls a dodgy dealer more reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: A loan shark is a moneylender charging huge interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant rates, the role of a loan shark.

clue.text: Nymph, therefore, occupying region

indicators.note: occupying means filling, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a region is an area
thus means therefore

explanation.surface: A nymph consequently takes over a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa is a nymph of Greek myth, turned into a spring.

clue.text: Conservative's position on board

explanation.surface: The Tory's seat on the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conventional and old-fashioned is called square, and a chessboard has 64 squares where pieces stand.

clue.text: Lacking support due, and in disarray without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
in disarray means in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Unsupported, the expected payment is chaotic and missing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; it means outside. 'in disarray' turns DUE AND into UNADED, which goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided means done without help from anyone.

clue.text: Theatrical melting-pot

parts.note: a vessel for melting metals that is also the name of a Sheffield theatre and an Arthur Miller play

explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a pot for melting metal, and also a famous play and a theatre.

clue.text: Mature in defeat, showing least fear

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: to best someone is to defeat them
old means mature, aged

explanation.surface: Someone experienced in losing is the most fearless.
explanation.definitionFit: The boldest person is the most daring and least afraid.

clue.text: Animal from British Columbia on board

indicators.note: on board a vessel means inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: what one boards is a boat
BC is the abbreviation for British Columbia, the Canadian province

explanation.surface: A Canadian creature is brought aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means inside the boat, so BC goes into BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American wild cat, a type of lynx.

clue.text: Indian jet base

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
the base of something is its foot

explanation.surface: An Indian aircraft's home airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests a plane; it is the black colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blackfoot are a Native American people of the northern plains.

clue.text: Left a fortune, taken back in tax

indicators.note: taken back means the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a lot means a large amount, a fortune

explanation.surface: A big inheritance was clawed back as tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns LLOT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a charge or levy, such as one paid on a road or bridge.

clue.text: A lot of fish caught were swimming in shoals

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
fish are said to run when they move upstream in shoals

explanation.surface: Many fish are netted as they swim in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is a Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a measure of herrings landed, so a quantity of fish.

clue.text: Language used in the course of your duties

indicators.note: in the course of means the letters are found running through these words

explanation.surface: A language spoken while you are at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also spoken in India.

clue.text: Cross-examiner

parts.note: not a lawyer questioning a witness but someone who inspects the crosses marked on voting papers

explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer checks ballot papers at an election count.

clue.text: Double act no longer appearing live

indicators.note: double means the piece is written out twice

parts.note: do means act, perform

explanation.surface: A comedy duo that no longer performs on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer appearing live' sounds like a retired act; it describes an extinct bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct bird, so none is still alive.

clue.text: Shattering in order to put right

indicators.note: in order says these letters must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Smashing something to fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a matter is to correct it or sort it out.
